diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, we can prove the desired result in the case of ${1}/{\gamma} >1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Positivity of the two gradient coefficients c_*-\frac{1}{\gamma}c^*\varepsilon_4^{-1} and \frac{1}{\gamma}(c_*-c^*\varepsilon_4) requires \varepsilon_4>\frac{c^*}{\gamma c_*} and \varepsilon_4<\frac{c_*}{c^*}, which is possible only if \gamma>(c^*/c_*)^2. The stated chain of inequalities contains no such condition, yet the lemma is asserted for all 0<1/\gamma<1 (i.e., all \gamma>1). For 1<\gamma\le(c^*/c_*)^2 no admissible \varepsilon_4 exists and the argument breaks down; the 'similarly' treated case 1/\gamma>1 analogously requires \gamma<(c_*/c^*)^2. Hence (a3.9) is not proved for 1/\gamma\in[(c_*/c^*)^2,(c^*/c_*)^2], a fixed neighbourhood of 1/\gamma=1, although the statement and the paper's scope cover all \gamma\ne1. (For the continuous form in Lemma lem2.1 the analogous condition is \varepsilon_4\in(1/\gamma,1), which needs no extra constraint; the gap is created solely by the stabilization constants c_*,c^* in (a3.7).)

failure_location.quote: Choose \(\frac{\beta k^2  c^*}{K-k^2\max\{n^*,1\} c^*} < \varepsilon_3 < \frac{K- \beta k^2  c^*}{\beta k^2  c^*}\) and \(\frac{1}{\gamma} < \frac{c^*}{\gamma c_*} < \varepsilon_4 < \frac{c_*}{c^*} < 1\), and we get \eqref{a3.9} immediately.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the hypothesis 1/\gamma<(c_*/c^*)^2 or 1/\gamma>(c^*/c_*)^2 (a limited weakening of the covered range), or choose/analyze the stabilizations so that c^*/c_* is close enough to 1 (e.g., c_*=c^*) to shrink the uncovered interval; covering the whole range with the given \mathds{T} would need a sharper absorption argument.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup condition and the well-posedness of the discrete source problem (a3.5) are established only for 1/\gamma bounded away from 1 by a margin depending on c^*/c_*. Consequently the error estimates of Lemmas lem3.3-lem3.4 and the eigenvalue/eigenfunction theorems th3.1 and thm:added-1 are proved only on that restricted range, not on the full advertised natural-materials regime 1/\gamma>0, 1/\gamma\ne1.
issues.title: Discrete T-coercivity proof requires an unstated constraint on gamma; the range near 1/gamma=1 is not covered
issues.why_classification: The advertised scope is all \gamma\ne1 but the proof covers only a constant-dependent sub-range excluding a neighbourhood of \gamma=1; restoring the full range needs either a restricted hypothesis (losing part of the regime) or a nontrivial sharpening, while all downstream rates otherwise survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem3.3 estimates the source-problem error \mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}-\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_h, whereas the quantity to be absorbed here is \hat{\mathbf{U}}_h=\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_h-\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_I, which does not satisfy the same Galerkin orthogonality: a_h(\hat{\mathbf{U}}_h,\boldsymbol{\Psi}_h)=b_h(\mathbf{F},\boldsymbol{\Psi}_h)-a_h(\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_I,\boldsymbol{\Psi}_h) carries an extra consistency term. The duality argument of Lemma lem3.3 must be re-run for \hat{\mathbf{U}}_h (the extra term is bounded by the same h^r(\cdot)+h^{1+r}(\cdot) quantities via (a3.18)-(a3.19)), and only then does \|\hat{\mathbf{U}}_h\|_0^2\lesssim h^{2r}\|\hat{\mathbf{U}}_h\|_V^2+\cdots justify dropping the K\|\hat{\mathbf{U}}_h\|_0^2 terms. As written, the absorption rests on a misapplication of Lemma lem3.3.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, from Lemma \ref{lem3.3}, we know that $\{ \| \hat{w}_h \|_{0}^2 +  \| \hat{u}_h \|_{0}^2 \}$ is a higher-order term compared with $\{\| \hat{w}_h \|_{1}^2 +  \|\hat{u}_h \|_{1}^2 \}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the re-run of the Lemma lem3.3 duality argument for \hat{\mathbf{U}}_h=\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_h-\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_I, estimating the extra consistency term b_h(\mathbf{F},\boldsymbol{\Psi}_h)-a_h(\mathbf{U}^{\mathbf{F}}_I,\boldsymbol{\Psi}_h) by the same (a3.18)-(a3.19) bounds; the stated estimate (a3.20) then follows unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: A key absorption step in the proof of the energy estimate (a3.20) is not justified as written; the conclusion is unaffected because the same duality argument re-run for \hat{\mathbf{U}}_h yields the required higher-order bound with no change in the final rate.
issues.title: Unjustified absorption of the L2 term in the energy-error proof of Lemma lem3.4
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is a routine, local re-run of the paper's own duality estimate with an extra term of the same order; the statement, method, and rate of Lemma lem3.4 all survive, so the repair is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In \eqref{a3.28}, we recognize that the second term on the right-hand side is of higher order compared to the first term; therefore, we only need to estimate the first term on the right-hand side.

issues.failure_explanation: The first term of (a3.28) is expanded as I+II+III. The bound II\lesssim h^{2r+2\min(l,s)} does not follow from the (a3.18) argument: with the paper's own definition b_h^E(\varphi_h,\psi_h)=b^E(\Pi^0\varphi_h,\Pi^0\psi_h)+S_b^E((I-\Pi^0)\varphi_h,(I-\Pi^0)\psi_h), one obtains b^E(u_h^f,f^*)-b_h^E(u_h^f,f^*)=b^E((I-\Pi^0)u_h^f,(I-\Pi^0)f^*)+b^E(\Pi^0 u_h^f,f^*-\Pi^0 f^*)-S_b^E((I-\Pi^0)u_h^f,(I-\Pi^0)f^*), whose size is h^{1+r}(\|u_h^f\|_0+\|u_h^f\|_1)\|f^*\|_{1+r}\lesssim h^{1+r}\|\mathbf{F}\|\|\mathbf{F}^*\| (the factor h^{1+r} in (a3.18) comes from approximating the dual solution z_I, which is absent in II); the claimed exponent 2r+2\min(l,s)>1+r is not obtained. Likewise the (a3.19) argument applied to III=a_h(\mathbf{A}_h\mathbf{F},\mathbf{A}_h^*\mathbf{F}^*)-a(\mathbf{A}_h\mathbf{F},\mathbf{A}_h^*\mathbf{F}^*) gives only h^{r+\min(l,s)} (the first term of (a3.19) is O(h^r)), not h^{2\min(l,s)}. Hence the displayed argument yields at best |\lambda_j-\widehat\lambda_{j,h}|\lesssim h^{r+\min(l,s)}, strictly weaker than (a3.23) when r<\min(l,s), and the assertion that the second term of (a3.28) is of higher order is also incorrect (with the correct rates the second term h^{2r+2\min(l,s)} is the smaller one). The claimed rate is nevertheless true: the cited Babu\v{s}ka-Osborn Thm 7.2 applied to \mu=1/(\beta-\lambda) gives |\lambda_j-\widehat\lambda_{j,h}|\lesssim\|(T-T_h)|_{R(\lambda_j)}\|_0\|(T^*-T_h^*)|_{R^*(\lambda_j)}\|_0\lesssim h^{2(r+\min(l,s))}\le h^{2\min(l,s)} via (a3.27) and its adjoint analogue.

failure_location.quote: using the argument for \eqref{a3.18} we have $I\!I \lesssim h^{2r + 2 \min (l,s)}$; and using the argument for \eqref{a3.19} we also get $ I\!I\!I  \lesssim h^{2 \min (l,s)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the I+II+III rate analysis by the standard closing step of Babu\v{s}ka-Osborn Thm 7.2: bound the right-hand side of (a3.28) by \|(T-T_h)|_{R(\lambda_j)}\|_0\|(T^*-T_h^*)|_{R^*(\lambda_j)}\|_0 using (a3.27) together with its adjoint analogue (adjoint versions of Lemmas 3.3-3.4, which the paper only sketches), giving h^{2(r+\min(l,s))}\le h^{2\min(l,s)}, then convert from \mu=1/(\beta-\lambda) to \lambda.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the eigenvalue estimate (a3.23) in Theorem th3.1 is invalid as written: the rates asserted for the terms II and III are wrong, and the argument establishes at best h^{r+\min(l,s)}. The statement of (a3.23) itself is correct by the standard Babu\v{s}ka-Osborn product bound, so no downstream statement is invalidated, but the presented justification for the headline rate of the paper's main theorem does not go through.
issues.title: Incorrect intermediate rate estimates in the proof of the eigenvalue error bound (a3.23)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion and rate of (a3.23) survive via a standard, contained argument (the product bound already implicit in the cited Thm 7.2), so no mathematical content is lost; but the paper's own proof of its central estimate contains false intermediate rates and must be replaced by a nontrivial repair, which is more than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We compute the first five approximate eigenvalues of the problem using the VEM with degrees \(l=1\) and \(l=2\), and the results are listed in Tables \ref{tab10}-\ref{tab12}.
The first five approximate eigenvalues obtained by solving with VEM on the generated mesh $\widehat{\mathcal{T}_h^1}$.} \label{tab10}

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that a comparison with the exact modified transmission eigenvalues of [Liu2023] (Example 7-9) was made and that it 'indicates that our method is effective'. However, the source never states the reference exact eigenvalues, so the claimed comparison is not presented or verifiable anywhere in the paper; the numerical tables contain only the paper's own approximate values. The effectiveness conclusion for absorbing media therefore rests solely on the observed refinement behaviour of the approximations, not on the asserted exact-value comparison.

failure_location.quote: When $l=1$, we refer to the exact modified transmission eigenvalues given in Example 7-9 of \cite{Liu2023}. The comparison between Tables \ref{tab10}-\ref{tab12} and the results in \cite{Liu2023} indicates that our method is effective in computing the modified transmission eigenvalues with absorbing media.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either state the exact eigenvalues from [Liu2023] and tabulate the errors against them, or rephrase the claim to refer only to the observed convergence of the approximate eigenvalues under mesh refinement.
issues.overall_effect: Only the validation narrative of Example 4 is affected: the paper asserts an external exact-value comparison that is not shown; no formal result or table is mathematically invalidated.
issues.title: Asserted validation against exact eigenvalues of Liu2023 is never carried out
issues.why_classification: A short, local reporting repair (add the reference values or drop the comparison claim) fully resolves it; no mathematical result, rate, or guarantee is affected.
